# Overview

`AutomergeDocument` is the primary class for working with Automerge CRDT documents. It provides methods for creating documents, reading and writing data, managing history, synchronizing with peers, and persisting state.

The class implements `IDisposable` because it holds a native Rust resource. Always use a `using` statement.

```csharp
using Ray.Automerge;

using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
```

# Creation and Disposal

## Create

```csharp
public static AutomergeDocument Create(string? actorId = null)
```

Creates a new empty Automerge document.

**Parameters:**
- `actorId` — Optional actor identifier. If null, a random actor ID is generated. If a valid hex string, it is used directly as the Automerge actor. If a non-hex string, it is UTF-8 encoded and used as the actor bytes.

**Returns:** A new `AutomergeDocument`.

**Exceptions:**
- `AutomergeException` — If the actor ID is invalid.

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
using var docWithActor = AutomergeDocument.Create("my-app-device-1");
```

## Load

```csharp
public static AutomergeDocument Load(byte[] data)
```

Loads a document from binary data produced by `Save`.

**Parameters:**
- `data` — The binary document data. Must not be null or empty.

**Returns:** A new `AutomergeDocument` containing the loaded state.

**Exceptions:**
- `ArgumentNullException` — When `data` is null.
- `ArgumentException` — When `data` is empty.
- `AutomergeException` — When the data is invalid or corrupted.

```csharp
byte[] saved = originalDoc.Save();
using var restored = AutomergeDocument.Load(saved);
```

## LoadWithOptions

```csharp
public static AutomergeDocument LoadWithOptions(byte[] data, LoadOptions options)
```

Loads a document with configurable verification and error handling.

**Parameters:**
- `data` — The binary document data. Must not be null or empty.
- `options` — Load configuration. See `LoadOptions`.

**Returns:** A new `AutomergeDocument`.

**Exceptions:**
- `ArgumentNullException` — When `data` or `options` is null.
- `ArgumentException` — When `data` is empty.
- `AutomergeException` — When the data is invalid.

```csharp
var options = new LoadOptions
{
  VerificationMode = VerificationMode.NoCheck,
  OnPartialLoad = OnPartialLoad.Ignore
};
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.LoadWithOptions(saved, options);
```

## ActorId


# Commit and Rollback

## Commit

```csharp
public string? Commit(string? message = null, long? timestampMillis = null)
```

Commits all pending operations as a single change.

**Parameters:**
- `message` — Optional commit message describing the change.
- `timestampMillis` — Optional Unix timestamp in milliseconds. If null, Automerge uses its default.

**Returns:** The change hash as a lowercase hex string, or null if there were no pending operations.

```csharp
doc.PutString(root, "title", "Hello");
var hash = doc.Commit("Set title");
```

## Rollback

```csharp
public ulong Rollback()
```

Discards all uncommitted operations and returns the number of operations rolled back.

**Returns:** The number of operations that were rolled back.

```csharp
doc.PutString(root, "title", "mistake");
var count = doc.Rollback(); // count = 1, change discarded
```

## EmptyChange

```csharp
public string EmptyChange(string? message = null, long? timestampMillis = null)
```

Creates a commit with no operations. Useful for creating a merge point or recording metadata.

**Parameters:**
- `message` — Optional commit message.
- `timestampMillis` — Optional timestamp.

**Returns:** The change hash as a lowercase hex string.



# Overview

Marks are formatting annotations applied to ranges of text. Each mark has a name (e.g., `"bold"`, `"link"`), a value, and a start/end range. Marks are returned by `GetMarks` and appear on `AutomergeTextSpan.Marks`.

```csharp
  Console.WriteLine($"{mark.Name}: {mark.Start}-{mark.End} = {mark.Value.Kind}");
}
```

|-------|-------------|
| `Before` | The mark expands when text is inserted before the start of the marked range. |
| `After` | The mark expands when text is inserted after the end of the marked range. This is the default. |

## Choosing an Expand Mode

| Formatting Type | Recommended Mode | Reason |
|----------------|-----------------|--------|
| Inline (bold, italic) | `After` (default) | New text typed at the end continues the format |
| Links | `None` | New text should not automatically become part of the link |
| Block-level | `Before` | New content at the start inherits the block format |
| Comments / annotations | `None` | Annotations should not grow |

```csharp
doc.Mark(textId, 6, 11, "link", "https://example.com", ExpandMode.None);
```

# Complete Example

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
var root = doc.RootId;

// Diff the two versions
var patches = doc.Diff(v1, v2);

{

  Console.WriteLine($"{patch.Action.Kind} at {pathStr}");
}
```

# Overview

`DocHandle<T>` is the primary way to interact with documents managed by a `Repo`. It wraps an `AutomergeDocument` with a lifecycle state machine, change events, thread-safe access, and sync coordination. Handles are obtained from `Repo.Create`, `Repo.Find`, `Repo.Clone`, or `Repo.Import`.

```csharp
using Ray.Automerge.Repository;

var handle = repo.Create<object>();
handle.Change(doc =>
{
  doc.PutString(doc.RootId, "title", "Hello");
});
var document = handle.Doc();
```

**Namespace:** `Ray.Automerge.Repository`

# HandleState

```csharp
public enum HandleState
```

The lifecycle state of a document handle.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Idle` | Initial state before any loading begins |
| `Loading` | Document is being loaded from storage |
| `Requesting` | Document is being requested from the network |
| `Ready` | Document is loaded and ready for use |
| `Unloaded` | Document has been unloaded from memory |
| `Deleted` | Document has been deleted |
| `Unavailable` | Document could not be found from any source |

**State transitions:**

```
Idle → Loading → Ready
Idle → Loading → Requesting → Ready
Ready → Unloaded → Loading (reload)
Ready → Deleted
Requesting → Unavailable
```

`AutomergeDocument` and `AutomergeSyncState` implement `IDisposable` because they hold native (Rust) resources. Always use `using` statements:

# Key Hierarchy

Storage keys follow a hierarchical structure:


The storage subsystem uses this structure to:
1. Load all data for a document with a single prefix query

Understanding documents, actors, container types, and the Automerge data model

# Overview

This guide explains the fundamental concepts behind Ray.Toolkit.Automerge.

Understanding these concepts helps you design effective collaborative applications.

# Documents

An Automerge document is a container for your data. It tracks all changes made to that data over time.

## Creating Documents

You create a document using the static factory method:

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
```

You can optionally specify an actor ID during creation:

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create("user-alice-device-1");
```

## Document State

Documents maintain several pieces of state:

**Root Object** - Every document has a root map where you store top-level data.

**Actor ID** - Identifies who is making changes to this document.

**Pending Operations** - Changes you've made but haven't committed yet.

**Commit History** - All committed changes with their messages and metadata.

**Heads** - The latest commit hashes representing the current state.

# Doc Handles

When an Automerge document is managed by a repository you interact with it through a `DocHandle`. The handle serializes
access, tracks locally generated change bytes, raises notifications, and exposes helpers for feeding remote updates back
into the document. See the [Doc Handles](/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge/repo/doc-handles/) guide for details on coordinating repository-backed documents.

# Actors

An actor represents a user or device making changes to a document.

Each document has exactly one actor ID. When you sync documents, Automerge uses actor IDs to track who made which changes.

## Actor ID Format

Automerge generates random UUIDs as actor IDs by default:

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
Console.WriteLine(doc.ActorId); // Something like "a1b2c3d4..."
```

You can set custom actor IDs for easier debugging or tracking:

```csharp
doc.ActorId = "alice-laptop";
```

## Why Actor IDs Matter

Actor IDs help resolve conflicts. When two actors make concurrent changes, Automerge uses the actor ID as a tiebreaker in some situations.

They also help you track change provenance. You can see which actor made each modification.

# Container Types

Automerge provides three container types for organizing data:

## Map

Maps store key-value pairs, like a dictionary or object. The root of every document is a map.

Use maps when you need named fields:

```csharp
var root = doc.RootId;
doc.PutString(root, "username", "alice");
doc.PutInt64(root, "score", 100);
```

Maps support any string as a key. Values can be any supported data type or nested container.

## List

Lists store ordered sequences of items, like an array.

Use lists when order matters and you don't need named keys:

```csharp
var root = doc.RootId;
var tasks = doc.PutObject(root, "tasks", AutomergeContainerType.List);
doc.ListInsertString(tasks, 0, "Write documentation");
doc.ListInsertString(tasks, 1, "Review code");
```

Lists support insertion at any index. Concurrent insertions from different actors maintain their relative order in predictable ways.

## Text

Text containers provide special CRDT semantics for collaborative text editing.

Use text when multiple users might edit the same content simultaneously:

```csharp
var root = doc.RootId;
var description = doc.PutObject(root, "description", AutomergeContainerType.Text);
doc.SpliceText(description, 0, 0, "Hello, world!");
```

Text containers track character-level operations. When two users edit nearby text, Automerge merges their changes intelligently.

# Object IDs

Every container in an Automerge document has a unique identifier called an Object ID.

## Getting Object IDs

When you create a container, you receive its Object ID:

```csharp
var root = doc.RootId; // The root map's ID
var listId = doc.PutObject(root, "items", AutomergeContainerType.List); // New list's ID
```

You use these IDs to reference containers in subsequent operations:

```csharp
doc.ListInsertString(listId, 0, "first item");
```

## Object ID Lifetime

Object IDs remain valid for the lifetime of the document. You can store them and use them later.

However, they don't serialize to JSON. When you call `HydrateJson()`, you get the data values, not the internal Object IDs.

# Commits

Automerge uses an explicit commit model. Changes you make are pending until you commit them.

## Creating Commits

Call `Commit()` to finalize your changes:

```csharp
var hash = doc.Commit("Update user profile");
```

The method returns a commit hash. This hash uniquely identifies this set of changes.

## Commit Messages

Commit messages help you understand your change history:

```csharp
doc.Commit("Fix typo in description");
doc.Commit("Add user preferences");
doc.Commit("Update task priorities");
```

Messages are optional but recommended for debugging and auditing.

## Commit Timestamps

You can provide explicit timestamps:

```csharp
var timestamp = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds();
doc.Commit("Scheduled update", timestamp);
```

Without an explicit timestamp, Automerge uses the current time.

## Rollback

You can discard uncommitted changes:

```csharp
doc.PutString(root, "temp", "temporary value");
var count = doc.Rollback(); // Discards the PutString operation
```

The method returns the number of operations rolled back.

# Conflict-Free Merging

Automerge automatically merges concurrent changes without conflicts.

## How It Works

Each operation has a unique identifier combining the actor ID and a logical timestamp. When merging, Automerge uses these identifiers to determine operation order.

Different data types have different merge semantics:

**Last-Write-Wins** - For simple values like strings and numbers, the operation with the higher timestamp wins.

**Addition** - For counters, values add together.

**List Operations** - Insertions from different actors maintain their relative positions. Deletions apply regardless of other changes.

**Text Operations** - Character insertions and deletions merge character by character.

## Concurrent Edits Example

Two users edit different fields in the same document:

```csharp
// Alice's document
using var alice = AutomergeDocument.Create();
var aliceRoot = alice.RootId;
alice.PutString(aliceRoot, "title", "Project Plan");
alice.Commit("Alice: Add title");

// Bob's document (starts empty)
using var bob = AutomergeDocument.Create();
var bobRoot = bob.RootId;
bob.PutString(bobRoot, "author", "Bob");
bob.Commit("Bob: Add author");

// Sync them
var heads = alice.GetHeads();
var changes = bob.GetChanges(heads);
alice.ApplyChanges(changes);

// Alice's document now has both title and author
```

Both changes survive the merge because they modify different keys.

## Concurrent Updates to Same Key

When two actors update the same key, the later timestamp wins:

```csharp
// Both Alice and Bob update "status" at roughly the same time
alice.PutString(aliceRoot, "status", "in-progress");
bob.PutString(bobRoot, "status", "completed");

// After sync, one value wins based on timestamps and actor IDs
```

This is last-write-wins semantics. If you need different behavior, use counters or separate keys.

# Data Types

Automerge supports these primitive data types:

**String** - UTF-8 text values.

**Int64** - Signed 64-bit integers.

**UInt64** - Unsigned 64-bit integers.

**Double** - 64-bit floating-point numbers.

**Boolean** - True or false values.

**Timestamp** - Unix timestamps in milliseconds.

**Bytes** - Binary data.

**Null** - Explicit null values.

**Counter** - CRDT counters that add together during merges.

You can also use three container types (Map, List, Text) to create nested structures.

# Change Tracking

Automerge tracks every change with full history.

## Getting Heads

Heads represent the latest state:

```csharp
var heads = doc.GetHeads();
foreach (var head in heads)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Head: {head}");
}
```

Most documents have one head. Multiple heads appear temporarily during merges.

## Getting Changes

Retrieve all changes since a known state:

```csharp
var knownHeads = new[] { "abc123...", "def456..." };
var changes = doc.GetChanges(knownHeads);
```

This returns a list of binary change objects. You can send these to other peers for synchronization.

## Last Local Change

Get the most recent change made by this actor:

```csharp
var lastChange = doc.GetLastLocalChange();
if (lastChange != null)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Last change size: {lastChange.Length} bytes");
}
```

This helps implement efficient change notification systems.

# Document Lifecycle

## Creation

Start with a new document:

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
```

## Modification

Make changes and commit them:

```csharp
var root = doc.RootId;
doc.PutString(root, "field", "value");
doc.Commit("Update field");
```

## Synchronization

Exchange changes with other documents:

```csharp
var changes = doc.GetChanges(otherDoc.GetHeads());
otherDoc.ApplyChanges(changes);
```

## Persistence

Save the document to bytes:

```csharp
var bytes = doc.Save();
```

Load it back later:

```csharp
using var restored = AutomergeDocument.Load(bytes);
```

## Cleanup

Dispose of documents when done:

```csharp
doc.Dispose();
```

Or use a `using` statement for automatic disposal.

# Performance Considerations

## Commit Frequency

Each commit adds overhead. Batch related changes into single commits:

```csharp
// Good: One commit for related changes
doc.PutString(root, "first_name", "Alice");
doc.PutString(root, "last_name", "Smith");
doc.PutString(root, "email", "alice@example.com");
doc.Commit("Update user info");

// Less efficient: Many small commits
doc.PutString(root, "first_name", "Alice");
doc.Commit("Update first name");
doc.PutString(root, "last_name", "Smith");
doc.Commit("Update last name");
```

## Document Size

Large documents take longer to serialize and sync. Consider splitting very large datasets into multiple documents.

## Memory Management

Documents hold native resources. Always dispose of them:

```csharp
using var doc = AutomergeDocument.Create();
// Use the document
// Automatic disposal happens here
```

DocumentId, PeerId, StorageKey, AutomergeUrl, and SessionId — the identity types used across the Repo layer

# Overview

The Repo layer uses several strongly-typed identifiers to distinguish documents, peers,
storage locations, URLs, and sessions. All are lightweight `readonly record struct` types
with implicit string conversion, making them safe to use as dictionary keys and easy to
pass through APIs that expect strings.

| Type | Package | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| `DocumentId` | Repo.Abstractions | Identifies a document (Base58Check encoded) |
| `PeerId` | Repo.Abstractions | Identifies a network peer |
| `StorageKey` | Repo.Abstractions | Hierarchical key for storage operations |
| `AutomergeUrl` | Repo | URL representation with scheme and optional heads |
| `SessionId` | Repo.Abstractions | Identifies a session for ephemeral deduplication |

# DocumentId

A Base58Check-encoded identifier for Automerge documents. This mirrors the branded string
type from the TypeScript `automerge-repo` implementation.

## Encoding

DocumentId uses [Base58Check](https://en.bitcoin.it/wiki/Base58Check_encoding) encoding,
which provides:

- Human-readable output (no ambiguous characters like `0`/`O` or `l`/`1`)
- Built-in checksum for detecting typos and corruption
- Compact representation of binary data

The binary representation must be at least 16 bytes. By default, `Generate()` encodes
a random GUID (16 bytes).

## Creating a DocumentId

```csharp
// Generate a random document ID
var docId = DocumentId.Generate();
// Example: "4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu"

// From a known string value
var docId = DocumentId.Parse("4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu");

// From binary data (at least 16 bytes)
var bytes = new byte[16];
RandomNumberGenerator.Fill(bytes);
var docId = DocumentId.FromBinary(bytes);
```

## Parsing and Validation

```csharp
// Parse with exception on failure
var docId = DocumentId.Parse("4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu");

// Safe parsing
if(DocumentId.TryParse("4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu", out var docId))
{
  // Valid
}

// Validation only
bool isValid = DocumentId.IsValid("4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu");
```

`TryParse` returns `false` for null, whitespace, invalid Base58 characters, failed checksum,
or binary data shorter than 16 bytes.

## Binary Conversion

```csharp
var docId = DocumentId.Generate();

// To binary
byte[] bytes = docId.ToBinary();

// From binary
var restored = DocumentId.FromBinary(bytes);
// restored == docId
```

Also available as static methods: `DocumentId.ToBinary(docId)` and `DocumentId.ToBinary(string)`.

## String Conversion

`DocumentId` has implicit operators for bidirectional string conversion:

```csharp
// Implicit to string
DocumentId docId = DocumentId.Generate();
string value = docId; // implicit conversion

// Implicit from string (calls Parse, throws on invalid)
DocumentId docId = "4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu";
```

This allows seamless interop with APIs that use plain strings.

## API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Value` | The Base58Check-encoded string |
| `Generate()` | Create a random DocumentId from a GUID |
| `FromBinary(byte[])` | Encode binary data (minimum 16 bytes) |
| `FromBinary(ReadOnlySpan)` | Span overload |
| `ToBinary()` | Decode to binary |
| `Parse(string)` | Parse with exception on failure |
| `TryParse(string, out DocumentId)` | Safe parse attempt |
| `IsValid(string)` | Validate without exceptions |
| `implicit operator string` | Convert to string |
| `implicit operator DocumentId` | Convert from string (calls Parse) |

# PeerId

A unique identifier for a peer in the network. Each Repo instance generates a `PeerId`
on startup.

## Format

The format is `"peer-{random}"` where `{random}` is the first 8 hex characters of a GUID:

```csharp
var peerId = PeerId.Generate();
// Example: "peer-a1b2c3d4"
```

This mirrors the TypeScript implementation which uses `Math.random().toString(36).slice(4)`.

## Usage

```csharp
// Generate
var peerId = PeerId.Generate();

// From known value
var peerId = new PeerId("peer-alice");

// Implicit string conversion
string value = peerId;        // "peer-alice"
PeerId fromStr = "peer-bob";  // implicit from string
```

## API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `PeerId(string)` | Constructor (throws if null/whitespace) |
| `Generate()` | Create with format `"peer-{8-hex-chars}"` |
| `implicit operator string` | Convert to string |
| `implicit operator PeerId` | Convert from string |
| `ToString()` | Returns the string value |

# StorageKey

A hierarchical key for organizing data in storage adapters. Each key consists of ordered
string components that form a path-like structure.

## Factory Methods

StorageKey provides purpose-specific factories for common storage patterns:

```csharp
// Document snapshot: [documentId, "snapshot", snapshotHash]
var key = StorageKey.DocumentSnapshot("abc123", "hash456");

// Incremental change: [documentId, "incremental", changeHash]
var key = StorageKey.DocumentIncremental("abc123", "hash789");

// Sync state: [documentId, "sync-state", storageId]
var key = StorageKey.DocumentSyncState("abc123", "storage-1");

// Generic: [namespace, key]
var key = StorageKey.Generic("metadata", "config");
```

## Prefix Matching

`StartsWith` enables hierarchical filtering for range operations:

```csharp
var prefix = new StorageKey(new[] { "abc123" });

var snapshotKey = StorageKey.DocumentSnapshot("abc123", "hash456");
snapshotKey.StartsWith(prefix); // true

var otherKey = StorageKey.DocumentSnapshot("xyz789", "hash456");
otherKey.StartsWith(prefix); // false
```

This is used by `IStorageAdapter.LoadRange` and `RemoveRange` to find all data for a
specific document.

## Debug Representation

```csharp
var key = StorageKey.DocumentSnapshot("abc123", "hash456");
key.ToDebugString(); // "abc123/snapshot/hash456"
key.ToString();      // same as ToDebugString()
```

## API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Components` | The ordered key components |
| `StorageKey(IReadOnlyList)` | Constructor from components |
| `DocumentSnapshot(docId, hash)` | Factory: `[docId, "snapshot", hash]` |
| `DocumentIncremental(docId, hash)` | Factory: `[docId, "incremental", hash]` |
| `DocumentSyncState(docId, storageId)` | Factory: `[docId, "sync-state", storageId]` |
| `Generic(namespace, key)` | Factory: `[namespace, key]` |
| `StartsWith(prefix)` | Check hierarchical prefix match |
| `ToDebugString()` | Components joined with `"/"` |

# AutomergeUrl

A static utility class for working with Automerge URLs. The URL format is:

```
automerge:<documentId>[#head1|head2|...]
```

Examples:

- `automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu`
- `automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu#head1|head2`

## Parsing

```csharp
var parsed = AutomergeUrl.Parse("automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu#head1|head2");

DocumentId docId = parsed.DocumentId;
IReadOnlyList<string>? heads = parsed.Heads; // ["head1", "head2"]
```

`Parse` throws `FormatException` if the URL does not start with `automerge:` or contains
an invalid document ID.

## Formatting

```csharp
// Without heads
string url = AutomergeUrl.Format(docId);
// "automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu"

// With heads
string url = AutomergeUrl.Format(docId, new[] { "head1", "head2" });
// "automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu#head1|head2"
```

## Generating and Validating

```csharp
// Generate a new URL with a random document ID
string url = AutomergeUrl.Generate();

// Validate without throwing
bool isValid = AutomergeUrl.IsValid("automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu");

// Extract just the document ID
DocumentId docId = AutomergeUrl.GetDocumentId("automerge:4NMNnkMhL8jXrdJ9jamS58PAVdXu");
```

## ParsedAutomergeUrl

The result of `Parse`:

```csharp
public sealed record ParsedAutomergeUrl(
  DocumentId DocumentId,
  IReadOnlyList<string>? Heads);
```

`Heads` is `null` when no fragment is present in the URL.

## API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Parse(string)` | Parse URL into DocumentId and optional heads |
| `Format(DocumentId, heads?)` | Format into URL string |
| `Format(string, heads?)` | String-based overload |
| `Generate()` | New URL with random DocumentId |
| `IsValid(string)` | Validate without exceptions |
| `GetDocumentId(string)` | Extract DocumentId from URL |

# SessionId

Identifies a transient session for ephemeral message deduplication. A new `SessionId` is
generated each time a peer starts — it does not persist across restarts.

## Purpose

The `NetworkSubsystem` uses `SessionId` together with a message counter to build deduplication
keys in the format `peerId:sessionId:count`. This prevents the same ephemeral message from
being processed multiple times when it arrives through different network adapters.

## Usage

```csharp
var sessionId = SessionId.Generate();
// Example: "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6" (32 hex chars, GUID "N" format)
```

## API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `SessionId(string)` | Constructor (throws if null/whitespace) |
| `Generate()` | Create from GUID in "N" format (32 hex chars) |
| `implicit operator string` | Convert to string |

Manage document lifecycle, persistence, and synchronization with the Repo pattern

# Overview

The Repository layer (`Ray.Automerge.Repo`) builds on top of `AutomergeDocument` to provide a complete
document management system. It handles persistence, network synchronization, peer discovery, and document
lifecycle — things you would otherwise need to implement yourself.

When working with raw `AutomergeDocument`, you are responsible for saving documents to disk, loading them
back, generating sync messages, managing peer connections, and tracking which changes have been sent to
whom. The Repo layer handles all of this automatically through pluggable adapters.

# When to Use Repo vs Standalone Documents

**Use `AutomergeDocument` directly when:**

- You need full control over persistence and sync timing
- You are building a custom sync protocol
- You have a single-user, single-device application
- You want minimal dependencies

**Use `Repo` when:**

- Multiple peers need to synchronize documents
- You want automatic persistence with configurable storage backends
- You need document lifecycle management (create, find, delete, clone)
- You are building a collaborative application

# Architecture

The Repo coordinates three subsystems through a single entry point:

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          Repo                                 │
│   Create / Find / Delete / Clone / Export / Import / Flush    │
├─────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┤
│  Storage    │   Network            │   Synchronizer           │
│  Subsystem  │   Subsystem          │   (CollectionSynchronizer│
│             │                      │    + DocSynchronizer)    │
├─────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┤
│ IStorage-   │ INetworkAdapter      │ Automerge sync protocol  │
│ Adapter     │ (one or more)        │ (generate/receive msgs)  │
│             │                      │                          │
│ • InMemory  │ • InMemory           │ Manages per-peer and     │
│ • FileSystem│ • SignalR             │ per-document sync state  │
│ • (custom)  │ • Orleans            │                          │
│             │ • (custom)           │                          │
└─────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┘
```

**StorageSubsystem** manages document persistence with automatic compaction. It saves a full snapshot
on the first write, then stores incremental changes. When the number of incremental chunks reaches the
size of the snapshot, it compacts everything into a new snapshot.

**NetworkSubsystem** manages one or more network adapters and routes messages between peers. It handles
peer discovery, connection lifecycle, and message deduplication for ephemeral messages.

**CollectionSynchronizer** orchestrates the Automerge sync protocol across all documents and peers.
When a document changes, it generates sync messages for each connected peer. When a sync message arrives,
it applies it to the correct document and updates sync state.

# Key Concepts

## DocHandle

Every document in the Repo is wrapped in a `DocHandle<T>`. Handles provide:

- Serialized access to the document (no concurrent mutation bugs)
- Change tracking (local changes are queued for sync)
- Event notifications (`Changed`, `HeadsChanged`, `Ready`, `Deleted`)
- State machine lifecycle (`Idle` → `Loading` → `Ready`)

See the [Doc Handles](/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge/repo/doc-handles/) guide for details.

## Document Identity

Documents are identified by `DocumentId`, a Base58Check-encoded identifier. The Repo generates these
automatically when you call `Create()`, or you can supply your own.

## Peer Identity

Each Repo instance has a unique `PeerId` (formatted as `peer-{random}`). This identity is used to
track which changes came from which peer and to manage sync state.

How CollectionSynchronizer and DocSynchronizer orchestrate the Automerge sync protocol across peers

# Overview

The synchronizer layer sits between the Repo and the network, orchestrating Automerge's
sync protocol for every document with every connected peer. It consists of two classes:

- **CollectionSynchronizer** — manages all documents in a repository, routes messages, enforces policies
- **DocSynchronizer** — manages sync for a single document across multiple peers

Both are internal to the `Ray.Automerge.Repo` package. You interact with them indirectly through
the [Repo](/Ray.Toolkit.Automerge/repo/getting-started/) API. This page documents how they work
for understanding sync behavior, debugging, and contributing.

# Architecture

```
Repo
 │
 ├─ CollectionSynchronizer
 │    ├─ DocSynchronizer (document A)
 │    │    ├─ AutomergeSyncState (peer 1)
 │    │    ├─ AutomergeSyncState (peer 2)
 │    │    └─ AutomergeSyncState (peer N)
 │    ├─ DocSynchronizer (document B)
 │    │    └─ ...
 │    └─ DocSynchronizer (document N)
 │         └─ ...
 │
 └─ NetworkSubsystem
      ├─ INetworkAdapter (SignalR)
      ├─ INetworkAdapter (InMemory)
      └─ INetworkAdapter (custom)
```

Each `DocSynchronizer` holds a separate `AutomergeSyncState` per peer. This enables efficient
incremental synchronization — only changes the remote peer has not seen are transmitted.

# Event Flow

## Incoming Message

When a message arrives from the network:

```
Network Adapter
  │  MessageReceived event
  ▼
NetworkSubsystem
  │  Deduplicates ephemeral messages
  │  MessageReceived event
  ▼
Repo handler
  │
  ▼
CollectionSynchronizer.OnMessageReceived(message)
  │  Check denylist
  │  Check access policy
  │  Create DocSynchronizer if needed
  │  Trigger document discovery if unknown
  ▼
DocSynchronizer.ReceiveMessage(message, senderId)
  │  Route by message type:
  │  ├─ SyncMessage      → apply sync protocol, respond
  │  ├─ RequestMessage    → mark peer as Wants, respond
  │  ├─ DocUnavailable    → update peer status
  │  └─ DocSnapshot       → load full document
  ▼
MessageToSend event → NetworkSubsystem → Network
SyncStateChanged event → StorageSubsystem (persist)
```

## Local Document Change

When you modify a document locally:

```
DocHandle.ChangeAsync(...)
  │
  ▼
Repo.NotifyDocumentChanged(documentId)
  │
  ▼
CollectionSynchronizer.NotifyDocumentChanged(documentId)
  │
  ▼
DocSynchronizer.NotifyLocalChange()
  │  For each active peer:
  │    GenerateSyncMessage → MessageToSend event
  ▼
NetworkSubsystem.Send → Network Adapters
```

## Peer Connection

When a new peer connects:

```
Network Adapter
  │  PeerCandidate event
  ▼
NetworkSubsystem
  │  PeerCandidate event
  ▼
Repo handler
  │
  ▼
CollectionSynchronizer.OnPeerConnected(peerId)
  │  Apply share policy to each registered document
  │  For each eligible document:
  │    DocSynchronizer.BeginSync(peerId)
  │      → SendSyncMessage → MessageToSend event
```

# CollectionSynchronizer

The collection-level synchronizer manages all documents and all peers. It is the primary
interface between the Repo and the sync protocol.

## Responsibilities

- Routes incoming messages to the correct `DocSynchronizer` by document ID
- Manages peer connections (connect/disconnect lifecycle)
- Enforces share and access policies
- Handles document discovery when receiving messages for unknown documents
- Maintains a denylist of documents that should never sync

## Key Methods

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `AddDocument(documentId)` | Register a document for sync with all connected peers |
| `RemoveDocument(documentId)` | Unregister a document and dispose its synchronizer |
| `OnPeerConnected(peerId)` | Begin syncing all eligible documents with the new peer |
| `OnPeerDisconnected(peerId)` | End sync for all documents with the disconnected peer |
| `OnMessageReceived(message)` | Route message to appropriate DocSynchronizer |
| `NotifyDocumentChanged(documentId)` | Push local changes to all syncing peers |
| `SetSharePolicy(policy)` | Control which documents are shared with which peers |
| `SetAccessPolicy(policy)` | Control which peers can access which documents |

## Events

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `MessageToSend` | A sync message needs to be sent to a peer (forwarded from DocSynchronizer) |
| `SyncStateChanged` | Sync state changed and should be persisted (forwarded from DocSynchronizer) |
| `MetricsUpdated` | Sync metrics updated for monitoring (forwarded from DocSynchronizer) |

## Document Discovery

When `OnMessageReceived` encounters a message for an unknown document:

1. Creates a new `DocSynchronizer` for the document
2. Calls the `requestDocument` callback so the Repo can check storage or ask other peers
3. Begins sync with the sender
4. Processes the message

This enables peers to discover documents they do not yet have. The Repo decides whether to
accept or reject the document based on application logic.

## Share and Access Policies

Both policies are async functions that return `bool`:

```csharp
// Only share documents in the "public" namespace
synchronizer.SetSharePolicy(async (documentId, peerId) =>
{
  return documentId.Value.StartsWith("public-");
});

// Only allow authenticated peers
synchronizer.SetAccessPolicy(async (documentId, peerId) =>
{
  return await authService.IsAuthenticated(peerId);
});
```

| Policy | Default | Controls |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Share policy | Share all | Which documents are proactively sent to which peers on connect |
| Access policy | Allow all | Which incoming messages are accepted from which peers |

When a share policy returns `false`, the document is not synced with that peer on connection.
When an access policy returns `false`, incoming messages from that peer for that document are silently dropped.

## Denylist

The denylist is a set of document IDs that are never synchronized, regardless of policies:

```csharp
var denylist = new HashSet<string> { "secret-doc-id" };
var synchronizer = new CollectionSynchronizer(
  getDocument, updateDocument, getPeerMetadata, requestDocument,
  denylist: denylist);
```

Denylisted documents are silently ignored for both incoming and outgoing sync.

# DocSynchronizer

The document-level synchronizer manages sync for a single document across multiple peers.
It is `internal` to the Repo package.

## Responsibilities

- Maintains per-peer `AutomergeSyncState` instances
- Generates and processes Automerge sync protocol messages
- Tracks peer document status (Unknown, Has, Wants, Unavailable)
- Sends the appropriate message type based on local and remote state
- Fires events for the CollectionSynchronizer to forward

## Peer Document Status

The synchronizer tracks what it knows about each peer's relationship with the document:

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `Unknown` | Initial state. We do not know if the peer has this document |
| `Has` | The peer has the document and can participate in sync |
| `Wants` | The peer has requested the document (sent a `RequestMessage`) |
| `Unavailable` | The peer indicated the document is unavailable |

Status transitions:

```
Unknown ──────> Has          (received sync data from peer)
Unknown ──────> Wants        (received request from peer)
Unknown ──────> Unavailable  (received doc-unavailable)
Wants ────────> Has          (sync completed after request)
```

## Message Handling

### SyncMessage (incoming)

When a `SyncMessage` arrives from a peer:

1. Get (or create) the local document
2. Get (or create) the sync state for this peer
3. Apply the sync message using `doc.ReceiveSyncMessage(syncState, data)`
4. Update the local document via callback
5. Set peer status to `Has`
6. Fire `SyncStateChanged` for persistence
7. Generate and send a response sync message

### RequestMessage (incoming)

When a `RequestMessage` arrives (peer wants the document):

1. Set peer status to `Wants`
2. If we do not have the document, send `DocumentUnavailableMessage`
3. Otherwise, process as a sync message (request carries initial sync state)

### DocumentSnapshotMessage (incoming)

When a full document snapshot arrives:

1. Load the document from the snapshot bytes
2. Update the local document via callback
3. Reset the sync state for this peer
4. Set peer status to `Has`

### Sending Messages

When `SendSyncMessage` is called (either initially or in response to incoming data):

1. If we do not have the document locally, send a `RequestMessage`
2. If `GenerateSyncMessage` returns data, send a `SyncMessage`
3. If `GenerateSyncMessage` returns null and the peer does not have the document, send a `DocumentSnapshotMessage` (full save)
4. If `GenerateSyncMessage` returns null and the peer already has the document, sync is complete

## Sync Protocol Loop

The Automerge sync protocol converges through message exchanges:

```
Peer A                                    Peer B
  │                                          │
  │  BeginSync → SendSyncMessage             │
  │  ──────────────────────────────────────> │
  │                                          │  ReceiveSyncMessage
  │                                          │  → SendSyncMessage (response)
  │  <────────────────────────────────────── │
  │  ReceiveSyncMessage                      │
  │  → SendSyncMessage (response)            │
  │  ──────────────────────────────────────> │
  │                                          │  ReceiveSyncMessage
  │                                          │  → GenerateSyncMessage returns null
  │          (converged — sync complete)     │
```

Each round, `GenerateSyncMessage` produces progressively smaller payloads as peers
converge. When it returns `null`, the sync is complete for that direction.

## NotifyLocalChange

When a document is modified locally, `NotifyLocalChange` sends updated sync messages
to all active peers:

```csharp
// Called by CollectionSynchronizer when Repo detects a local change
docSync.NotifyLocalChange();
// → For each active peer: GenerateSyncMessage → MessageToSend event
```

# NetworkSubsystem

The `NetworkSubsystem` manages multiple network adapters and coordinates message delivery:

- Routes outgoing messages through the appropriate adapter
- Forwards incoming messages from all adapters to the synchronizer
- Tracks peer-to-adapter mappings
- Deduplicates ephemeral messages across adapters
- Stores peer metadata

## Ephemeral Deduplication

When multiple adapters are active, the same ephemeral message could arrive through different
transports. The NetworkSubsystem tracks seen messages using a key of
`peerId:sessionId:count` and keeps the last 1000 entries to prevent gossip loops.

## Adapter Readiness

The `WhenReady` method returns a `Task` that completes when at least one adapter is ready.
This is used during document discovery to ensure the network is available before requesting
documents from peers.

# Thread Safety

Both synchronizers use `SemaphoreSlim(1,1)` to protect mutable state. Events are collected
in a `List<Action>` during lock-held operations and fired **after** the lock is released.
This deferred event pattern prevents deadlocks when event handlers call back into the
synchronizer.

```
lock.Wait()
try
{
  // Mutate state
  // Collect events: deferredEvents.Add(() => Event?.Invoke(...))
}
finally
{
  lock.Release()
}

// Fire all events outside the lock
foreach(var action in deferredEvents)
{
  action();
}
```

Operations that call `BeginSync` (which acquires the DocSynchronizer's own lock) are also
performed outside the CollectionSynchronizer's lock to avoid nested lock acquisition.

# Overview

When a user types at the edge of a formatted range, should the new character inherit the formatting? The answer depends on the context:

- Typing at the end of a **bold** word should probably continue bold.
- Typing at the end of a **link** should probably *not* extend the link.

`ExpandMode` controls this boundary behavior. It determines whether a mark "expands" to cover newly inserted characters at its start or end.

# The ExpandMode Enum

```csharp
public enum ExpandMode
{
    Before,  // Expands when text is inserted before the start
    After,   // Expands when text is inserted after the end (default)
    Both,    // Expands at both boundaries
    None     // Never expands
}
```

# Specifying an Expand Mode

Pass an `ExpandMode` as the last parameter to `Mark`:

```csharp
// Bold expands at both ends (typing continues the bold)
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 5, "bold", true, ExpandMode.Both);

// Link never expands (typing at edges is not part of the link)
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 10, "link", "https://example.com", ExpandMode.None);
```

If you omit the expand mode, Automerge uses `ExpandMode.After` as the default.

# Boundary Behavior

## ExpandMode.None

The mark never expands. Characters inserted at either boundary are **not** covered by the mark.

```
Before insert:  [bold: "Hello"] World
                 ▲0          ▲5

Insert "X" at index 5 (end boundary):

After insert:   [bold: "Hello"]X World
                 ▲0          ▲5▲6

"X" is NOT bold — the mark stayed at [0..5]
```

```csharp
doc.SpliceText(textId, 0, 0, "Hello World");
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 5, "bold", true, ExpandMode.None);
doc.Commit("mark bold none");

// Insert at the end boundary
doc.SpliceText(textId, 5, 0, "X");
doc.Commit("insert at boundary");
// "X" is not bold
```

**Use for**: Links, comments, annotations — anything that shouldn't grow when users type adjacent to it.

## ExpandMode.After

The mark expands when text is inserted **after** the end boundary. Characters inserted at the start boundary are not covered.

```
Before insert:  [bold: "Hello"] World
                 ▲0          ▲5

Insert "X" at index 5 (end boundary):

After insert:   [bold: "HelloX"] World
                 ▲0           ▲6

"X" IS bold — the mark expanded to [0..6]
```

**Use for**: Inline formatting (bold, italic) where continuing to type should maintain the format. This is the default behavior.

## ExpandMode.Before

The mark expands when text is inserted **before** the start boundary. Characters inserted at the end boundary are not covered.

```
Before insert:  Hello [italic: "World"]
                       ▲6          ▲11

Insert "X" at index 6 (start boundary):

After insert:   Hello [italic: "XWorld"]
                       ▲6           ▲12

"X" IS italic — the mark expanded backward
```

**Use for**: Rare cases where prepending should inherit formatting but appending should not.

## ExpandMode.Both

The mark expands at both boundaries. Any character inserted at either edge is covered.

```
Before insert:  [bold: "Hello"] World
                 ▲0          ▲5

Insert "X" at index 5 (end boundary):

After insert:   [bold: "HelloX"] World
                 ▲0           ▲6

Insert "Y" at index 0 (start boundary):

After insert:   [bold: "YHelloX"] World
                 ▲0            ▲7

Both "X" and "Y" are bold
```

```csharp
doc.SpliceText(textId, 0, 0, "Hello World");
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 5, "bold", true, ExpandMode.Both);
doc.Commit("mark bold both");

// Insert at the end boundary
doc.SpliceText(textId, 5, 0, "X");
doc.Commit("insert at boundary");
// "X" is bold
```

**Use for**: Block-level formatting or cases where the mark should aggressively include adjacent text.

# Choosing the Right Mode

| Formatting Type | Recommended Mode | Reasoning |
|----------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Bold, Italic, Underline | `After` or `Both` | Continuing to type should maintain the format |
| Links | `None` | Typing next to a link shouldn't extend it |
| Comments / Annotations | `None` | Annotations have fixed boundaries |
| Highlight | `Both` | Highlighted region grows with adjacent edits |
| Font Size | `After` | Typing continues at the same size |
| Code spans | `None` | Code boundaries are explicit |
| Block quotes | `Both` | Content added at edges belongs to the block |

# Expand Mode with Unmark

`Unmark` also accepts an expand mode to control how the unmarked region behaves:

```csharp
doc.Unmark(textId, "bold", 0, 11, ExpandMode.None);
```

# Concurrent Edits and Expand Modes

Expand modes work correctly with concurrent edits from multiple peers. If Peer A marks a range with `ExpandMode.None` and Peer B inserts text at the boundary, the inserted text won't receive the mark — even after merging.

This is a key part of the [Peritext](https://www.inkandswitch.com/peritext/) model: expand modes encode the user's intent about boundary behavior, and that intent is preserved through merges.

# Overview

Automerge's text containers support more than plain text. Through **marks**, you can attach formatting annotations (bold, italic, links, font size) to ranges of text — and these annotations merge correctly across concurrent edits from multiple peers.

This rich text model is based on [Peritext](https://www.inkandswitch.com/peritext/), a CRDT algorithm designed specifically for collaborative rich text editing. Peritext defines how formatting operations compose, overlap, and resolve conflicts in a multi-user environment.

# Core Concepts

## Marks

A **mark** is a named annotation applied to a range of characters in a text container. Marks have:

- **Name** — A string identifier (e.g., `"bold"`, `"italic"`, `"link"`, `"fontSize"`)
- **Value** — A boolean, string, or integer value
- **Range** — A start and end index within the text

```csharp
// Mark characters 0–5 as bold
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 5, "bold", true);

// Mark characters 6–11 as a link
doc.Mark(textId, 6, 11, "link", "https://example.com");

// Mark characters 0–10 with a font size
doc.Mark(textId, 0, 10, "fontSize", 24L);
```

Marks are stored as CRDT operations. They merge correctly when concurrent edits arrive from other peers.

## Spans

A **span** is a segment of text with its associated marks. When you read rich text, you get a list of spans — each span contains the text content and the marks that apply to it.

```
Text:   "Hello World"
Marks:  bold on [0..5]

Spans:  [AutomergeTextSpan("Hello", marks: [bold=true]),
         AutomergeTextSpan(" World", marks: [])]
```

The `GetSpans` method splits text at mark boundaries, giving you the data needed to render formatted text.

## Blocks

A **block** is a structural marker that separates paragraphs, headings, or other block-level elements. Blocks are represented as `AutomergeBlockSpan` objects in the span list.

Blocks are an advanced feature for structured document editing. Most rich text use cases only need marks and spans.

# When to Use Rich Text

## Use Rich Text When:

**You need formatted collaborative text** — Multiple users editing a document with bold, italic, links, headings, or other formatting.

**Format and content change independently** — One user adds text while another formats a different section. Marks and text operations compose naturally.

**You want semantic annotations** — Attach metadata to text ranges (comments, highlights, review status) that survive concurrent edits.

## Use Plain Text When:

**No formatting needed** — Simple text fields like chat messages, notes, or code don't need marks.

**Performance matters** — Plain text operations (`SpliceText`) are lighter than maintaining marks. For high-throughput scenarios, keep things simple.

**Content is short and atomic** — Single-line fields (names, titles) rarely need rich text.

# Rich Text Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Mark / Unmark                           │  Write operations
│  doc.Mark(textId, start, end, name, val) │
│  doc.Unmark(textId, name, start, end)    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  GetMarks / GetSpans                     │  Read operations
│  doc.GetMarks(textId)                    │
│  doc.GetSpans(textId)                    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ExpandMode                              │  Boundary behavior
│  Before, After, Both, None               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Mark / Unmark** — Apply or remove formatting annotations on text ranges.
- **GetMarks** — Read all marks as a flat list with name, value, start, and end.
- **GetSpans** — Read text split at mark boundaries, each span carrying its marks.
- **ExpandMode** — Controls whether marks grow when text is inserted at their edges.

# Peritext Model

The [Peritext paper](https://www.inkandswitch.com/peritext/) defines how rich text formatting works in CRDTs. Key principles:

1. **Marks are independent operations** — Adding bold to "Hello" and italic to "World" are separate operations that compose without conflict.

2. **Same-name marks overwrite** — If two users mark the same range with different `"color"` values, the last-writer-wins per character.

3. **Different-name marks coexist** — A character can be both bold and italic simultaneously.

4. **Expand modes control boundary behavior** — When you insert a character at the edge of a bold range, should the new character be bold? `ExpandMode` answers this.

# How It Works

## Connection Flow

```
Client                          Server (DocumentsHub)
  │                                    │
  │  Connect(peerId, metadata)         │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────>│
  │     GetConnection()                │
  │     Register hub callbacks         │
  │     Handshake(PeerHandshakeDto)    │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────>│
  │                                    │  Store PeerId in Context.Items
  │                                    │  Broadcast OnPeerJoined to Others
  │  <─────────────────────────────────│
  │     Mark adapter ready             │
  │     Raise PeerCandidate event      │
```

1. The Repo calls `Connect` on the adapter with a `PeerId`
2. The adapter lazily creates the SignalR connection
3. It registers hub callbacks (`OnReceiveMessage`, `OnPeerJoined`, `OnPeerLeft`)
4. It sends a `Handshake` to the server with peer identity and metadata
5. The server stores the peer ID and broadcasts `OnPeerJoined` to all other connected clients
6. The adapter marks itself ready and raises `PeerCandidate`

## Message Flow

```
Sender                          Server                          Receiver
  │                                │                                │
  │  Send(SyncMessage)             │                                │
  │  ─────────────────────────────>│                                │
  │   auto-subscribe to group      │                                │
  │   SendMessage(MessageDto)      │                                │
  │  ─────────────────────────────>│                                │
  │                                │  AddToGroupAsync (auto-sub)    │
  │                                │  OthersInGroup.OnReceiveMessage│
  │                                │  ─────────────────────────────>│
  │                                │                                │  Deserialize
  │                                │                                │  Raise MessageReceived
```

1. The adapter serializes the `IRepoMessage` into a `MessageDto`
2. Auto-subscribes to the document group if not already subscribed
3. The server adds the sender to the group (idempotent) and broadcasts to `OthersInGroup`
4. Receiving clients deserialize the `MessageDto` back to the original message type
5. The `MessageReceived` event fires on a background thread to avoid blocking SignalR

## Document Groups

The server organizes connections into SignalR groups by document ID. When a client sends a sync message
for document `abc123`, the server:

1. Adds the sender to group `abc123` (auto-subscription)
2. Broadcasts the message to all other members of group `abc123`

This ensures only peers interested in a specific document receive its sync traffic.

## Peer Lifecycle

| Event | Trigger | Effect |
|-------|---------|--------|
| `OnPeerJoined` | Client sends `Handshake` | Server broadcasts to `Clients.Others` |
| `OnPeerLeft` | Client disconnects | Server broadcasts to `Clients.Others` |
| `OnReceiveMessage` | Client sends `SendMessage` | Server routes to `OthersInGroup` |

# Wire Protocol

## MessageDto

All messages are serialized as `MessageDto` using MessagePack:

```csharp
[MessagePackObject]
public readonly record struct MessageDto
{
  [Key(0)] public required string MessageType { get; init; }
  [Key(1)] public string? DocumentId { get; init; }
  [Key(2)] public required string SenderId { get; init; }
  [Key(3)] public required byte[] Data { get; init; }
}
```

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `MessageType` | One of: `"sync"`, `"request"`, `"doc-unavailable"`, `"doc-snapshot"` |
| `DocumentId` | Target document (used for group routing) |
| `SenderId` | Peer ID of the sender (prevents echo-back) |
| `Data` | Serialized Automerge sync protocol payload |

Sent during the initial `Handshake` call:

```csharp
{

}
```

The adapter deserializes incoming `MessageDto` into these `IRepoMessage` subtypes:

|-----------|---------|-------------|

| `"doc-snapshot"` | `DocumentSnapshotMessage` | Full document snapshot |
| `"ephemeral"` | (not yet supported) | Transient data (presence, cursors) |

# Thread Safety

- All adapter methods are protected by a `SemaphoreSlim(1,1)`
- Hub callbacks (`OnReceiveMessage`, `OnPeerJoined`, `OnPeerLeft`) dispatch events on background threads via `Task.Run` to avoid blocking SignalR
- Document subscriptions use `ConcurrentDictionary` for lock-free tracking
- The `SignalRConnectionService` lazily creates connections and reuses them

# Overview

`FileSystemStorageAdapter` persists document data to the local file system with an in-memory cache layer
for fast repeated reads. It uses directory sharding to prevent any single directory from accumulating too
many entries.

This adapter is in a separate package:

```bash
dotnet add package Ray.Automerge.Repo.Storage.FileSystem
```

# Basic Setup

```csharp
using Ray.Automerge.Repository;
using Ray.Automerge.Repository.Storage.FileSystem;

var storage = new FileSystemStorageAdapter("./data/automerge");

var repo = new Repo(new RepoConfig
{
  Storage = storage
});
```

The base directory is created automatically if it does not exist.

# Configuration Options

Pass `FileSystemStorageOptions` to customize caching behavior:

```csharp
var storage = new FileSystemStorageAdapter(
  "./data/automerge",
  new FileSystemStorageOptions
  {
    CacheSizeLimit = 200 * 1024 * 1024,          // 200 MB (default: 100 MB)
    CacheSlidingExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) // 10 min (default: 5 min)
  });
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `CacheSizeLimit` | `long` | 100 MB | Maximum total size of cached data in bytes |
| `CacheSlidingExpiration` | `TimeSpan` | 5 minutes | How long cached entries live without being accessed |

# Directory Structure

The adapter uses a sharding scheme to distribute files across directories. The first two characters
of the document ID become a parent directory, and the rest becomes a subdirectory:

```
StorageKey: ["abc123def", "snapshot", "hash456"]
File path:  baseDir/ab/c123def/snapshot/hash456

StorageKey: ["abc123def", "incremental", "hash789"]
File path:  baseDir/ab/c123def/incremental/hash789

StorageKey: ["abc123def", "sync-state", "peer-1"]
File path:  baseDir/ab/c123def/sync-state/peer-1
```

This sharding prevents file system performance degradation from too many entries in a single directory.
A typical directory tree looks like:

```
data/automerge/
├── ab/
│   └── c123def/
│       ├── snapshot/
│       │   └── hash456
│       ├── incremental/
│       │   ├── hash789
│       │   └── hash012
│       └── sync-state/
│           └── peer-1
├── xy/
│   └── z789ghi/
│       └── snapshot/
│           └── hash345
```

# Caching Behavior

The adapter wraps `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory.MemoryCache` for read performance:

1. **On Load** — checks the cache first. If the key is cached, returns immediately without disk I/O.
   On cache miss, reads from disk and populates the cache.
2. **On Save** — writes to disk and updates the cache simultaneously.
3. **On Remove** — removes from both the cache and disk.
4. **Cache eviction** — entries expire after `CacheSlidingExpiration` of inactivity. The total cache
   size is bounded by `CacheSizeLimit`.

## Cache Size Accounting

Each cached entry's size is set to the byte length of the stored data. The `MemoryCache` uses these
sizes to enforce the `CacheSizeLimit`. When the limit is reached, least-recently-used entries are
evicted.

# Thread Safety

The adapter uses a `SemaphoreSlim(1, 1)` to serialize file system operations. While the cache itself
is thread-safe, file system operations are serialized to prevent concurrent writes to the same file.

# Known Limitations

## RemoveRange Cache Behavior

When `RemoveRange` deletes a directory tree, it does not explicitly clear individual cache entries.
The `MemoryCache` API does not expose key enumeration, so cached entries for removed files remain
until they expire naturally via the sliding expiration window.

This means that after a `RemoveRange`, subsequent `Load` calls may return stale data from the cache
until the entries expire. If this is a concern, consider using a shorter `CacheSlidingExpiration` or
disposing and recreating the adapter.

## First Key Component Length

The first component of every `StorageKey` must be at least 2 characters long (for the shard split).
In practice, `DocumentId` values are always long enough, but custom keys should respect this constraint.

# Usage with Repo

```csharp
using Ray.Automerge.Repository;
using Ray.Automerge.Repository.Storage.FileSystem;

using var storage = new FileSystemStorageAdapter("./data/automerge");

var repo = new Repo(new RepoConfig
{
  Storage = storage,
  SaveDebounceRate = 200 // increase debounce to reduce disk writes
});

// Create and modify documents
var handle = repo.Create<AutomergeDocument>();
await handle.ChangeAsync(doc =>
{
  doc.PutString(doc.RootId, "title", "Persisted Document");
});

// Flush ensures data is on disk
await repo.Flush();

// Later, find the document (loads from disk on first access)
var found = await repo.Find<AutomergeDocument>(handle.DocumentId);
```

# Direct Usage

You can also use the adapter directly without a Repo, for low-level storage operations:

```csharp
using var storage = new FileSystemStorageAdapter("./data/test");

var key = StorageKey.DocumentSnapshot("doc-abc123", "hash-1");
await storage.Save(key, documentBytes);

var loaded = await storage.Load(key);
Assert.NotNull(loaded);

// Get chunk metadata without loading data
var prefix = new StorageKey(["doc-abc123"]);
var info = await storage.GetChunkInfo(prefix);
foreach(var chunk in info)
{
  Console.WriteLine($"{chunk.Key}: {chunk.Size} bytes");
}
```

# Disposal

Disposing the adapter releases the cache and semaphore. Files on disk are not deleted:

```csharp
storage.Dispose();
// Cache cleared, disk data remains
// Future operations throw ObjectDisposedException
```

# API Summary

| Member | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `Load(key)` | Load from cache or disk (returns null if missing) |
| `Save(key, data)` | Write to disk and update cache |
| `Remove(key)` | Delete from disk and cache |
| `LoadRange(prefix)` | Load all matching chunks from disk |
| `RemoveRange(prefix)` | Delete directory tree for prefix |
| `GetChunkInfo(prefix)` | Get file metadata without loading data |
| `Dispose()` | Release cache and semaphore (keeps files) |
